title: KV TTL compaction race -> handle buildup causing fragmentation and GPU OOMs (hosted + dedicated)
creator: Anika Rao
description: Summary: We received a multi-tenant escalation where both Hosted and several Dedicated pools experienced intermittent GPU OOMs during high-concurrency chat workloads. Investigation traced OOM triggers to a steady growth of stale KV cache handles after TTL expiration, which was not reclaimed promptly due to a race between async TTL sweeper and session handoff. The accumulation caused slab fragmentation and sudden large contiguous allocation failures on large-sequence inference, leading to OOM crashes and degraded tail latency. The issue manifested more frequently under bursty prefix-heavy workloads and long-lived sessions. This ticket tracks the diagnosis, emergency mitigations, runtime patch, rollout, and follow-up work.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate long-lived sessions with many unique prefixes and short TTLs (10-30s) while driving bursty concurrent generation requests (200-500 qps) against hosted/dedicated clusters.
Observe KV index growth and tombstone counts in /observability/kvcache/tombstones over 10-30 minutes.
Trigger large sequence generation (>=2048 tokens) to force large contiguous arena allocations and watch for allocation failures in runtime logs.
Reproduce via synthetic stress harness used in labs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-tests/kv_ttl_stress (internal)
Note: production reproduction required scaled concurrency and multi-tenant mix; single-tenant tests under-represent fragmentation impact.
root_cause: An async TTL compaction sweep used a best-effort tombstone marking path that could race with session handle reclamation. Under contention, tombstones were left referenced by stale session handles preventing free lists from being reclaimed. Over time this created many small unusable holes in GPU slab memory (fragmentation) and an inflated KV index. The runtime allocator then failed to find large contiguous blocks for long-sequence allocations, triggering GPU OOMs. Key contributing factors: (1) non-atomic TTL mark-and-sweep with delayed reclamation, (2) lack of backpressure on request admission when KV metadata exceeded thresholds, (3) slab compaction heuristics tuned for steady-state, not bursty workload patterns.
fix_summary: Shipping runtime-1.21 hotpatch: (A) Introduced epoch-based handle reclamation so that tombstone marking and handle invalidation are synchronized without global stalls. (B) Added an adaptive slab compaction heuristic triggered when tombstone density > 15% and contiguous free runs < threshold; compaction performs bounded background merges. (C) Emergency safety: per-pool KV metadata soft-throttling and prefix eviction (LRU with TTL awareness) to stop runaway growth while compaction runs. (D) Metrics and alerts: new kvcache.tombstone_ratio and allocator.contiguous_run_percent for early detection.
rollout_plan: 2026-03-09: Hotfix PR merged to release branch (PR# internal: 12874).
2026-03-09: Canary deploy to 5% of hosted candidate nodes + single Dedicated pilot customer cluster during off-peak window.
2026-03-10: Monitor 48h for tombstone_ratio, contiguous_run_percent, and GC pause times.
2026-03-11: Gradual ramp to 100% hosted and remaining Dedicated pools with 2-hour blast radius checks between waves.
Rollback plan: Toggle kvcache.adaptive_compact_enabled=false and re-enable pre-hotfix allocator if severe regressions; fallback image preserved.
qa_and_verification: Added deterministic unit tests for epoch reclamation and race scenarios (kv_epoch_reclaim_test).
End-to-end stress test included in CI nightly harness against a simulated multi-tenant load generator (passed 5m sustained run without tombstone growth).
Post-deploy validation: no GPU OOM alerts for 72 hours across previously affected clusters; tombstone_ratio stabilized < 8% within 20 minutes of rollout.
Manual verification: memory snapshot before/after compaction and allocator histograms (heap fragmentation metric) collected and reviewed by reliability team.
followups: ENG-99000: Improve admission control to backpressure at 60% kvcache metadata growth (tracking ticket).
ENG-99312: Evaluate per-tenant compaction quotas and rate-limited background compaction to reduce noisy neighbor impact.
DES-412: Console UX: surface kvcache.tombstone_ratio and suggested remediation steps in cluster health page.
PM-721: Review SLA crediting for impacted customers and communicate closure with support and success teams.
notes: We intentionally kept compaction bounded to avoid long GC stalls during peak latency windows; the heuristic trades immediate reclamation for latency stability.
Initial emergency mitigation (prefix eviction) was critical to stop OOM recurrence while compaction warmed up.

This root cause is different from previous 'kv-handle-leak' tickets: here the handles were not leaking forever but remained transiently referenced due to the async race, causing fragmentation rather than linear memory growth.
Recommend grooming a playbook for kvcache fragmentation incidents: detection thresholds, emergency mitigations, and rollback signals.
